# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision

The Conservatives present their manifesto as a continuation of economic recovery following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. They highlight falling inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), rising real wages, and returning growth as evidence their plan is working. The party commits to reducing borrowing and debt while maintaining fiscal rules.

## Key Tax Pledges

The centrepiece is cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual saving for average workers. For the self-employed, they promise to abolish the main rate of National Insurance entirely. The new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household system, with families keeping benefits until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Borders

The manifesto introduces a legally binding cap on migration, with annual parliamentary votes on levels. They commit to continuing Rwanda deportation flights and reforming international asylum rules. The party promises to end illegal migration through deterrence and tougher enforcement.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending will increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, described as the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The party emphasises continued support for Ukraine and maintaining the nuclear deterrent.

## Public Services

NHS spending will increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The party promises 40 new hospitals by 2030, expanded mental health support, and implementation of the NHS Long-Term Workforce Plan. Education pledges include protecting school funding and introducing the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Housing and Communities

The target is 1.6 million new homes, primarily on brownfield land, while protecting the Green Belt. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. The party promises 8,000 additional police officers and continued investment in local transport infrastructure.

## Energy and Environment

The Conservatives commit to net zero by 2050 through a "pragmatic" approach, including annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, trebling offshore wind capacity, and expanding nuclear power. They promise no new green levies on household bills.

## Social Policy

The manifesto introduces mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds, offering either military or civic service options. On gender issues, they pledge to clarify that "sex" in the Equality Act means biological sex, protecting single-sex spaces.
